title: Division invariant
statement: For lists $z$ and $S$ of Boolean digits, an invariant holds if there are lists $R$, $r$, and $q$ such that $S$ is the nested pair encoding of the second decoded component of $z$, followed by $R$, $r$, and $q$; both $r$ and $q$ have length at most the length of the first decoded component of $z$ minus the length of $R$. In addition, if the natural number represented by the second decoded component is positive, then $(\operatorname{val}(q)\operatorname{val}(b)+\operatorname{val}(r))2^{|R|}+\operatorname{val}(\operatorname{reverse}(R))=\operatorname{val}(a)$ and $\operatorname{val}(r)<\operatorname{val}(b)$, where $a$ and $b$ are the natural numbers represented by the first and second decoded components of $z$.

$|r|+|R|$ is at most the length of the first decoded component
$|q|+|R|$ is at most the length of the first decoded component
when the second decoded component has positive value, the stated reconstruction equality and remainder bound hold
